text:
Anika: Heads up — after the sticky-routing change last night we're seeing a persistent gap between console 'active_connections' and infra socket counts. Console ~2.4k, infra shows ~3.6k. Not a transient spike, it's steady for ~45m. Anyone else seeing this?

Leo: Hmm. Which metric exactly are you comparing? console UI active_connections vs edge socket gauge?

Anika: console route-level active_connections (per-route panel) vs edge-proxy socket_count aggregated by region (our /metrics endpoint). I attached a tiny log snippet below.

Jo: I think I hit this in staging — socket pool reuse + session handoff can leave a session_id flagged active even after client disconnects because the connection is returned to the pool and then reassigned. Console dedup logic assumes 1 socket == 1 session.

Neil: Are we certain it's pool reuse not duplicate session creation on reconnect? Any 4xx/5xx noise?

Anika: No large increase in 4xx/5xx. Here's sample from proxy trace:
```
[2026-03-23T01:12:03Z] socket_reuse=true session_id=abc123 route=eu-west client_closed=false
[2026-03-23T01:12:03Z] assign_socket socket_id=pool-7 session_id=abc123 route=eu-west
[2026-03-23T01:12:10Z] client_disconnect socket_id=pool-7 session_id=abc123
[2026-03-23T01:12:12Z] assign_socket socket_id=pool-7 session_id=def456 route=eu-west
```
Looks like the pool reuses socket_id=pool-7 between sessions. Console records session_id -> active but maps it to socket_count TTL differently.

Sarah: If true, console should surface a `socket_pool_reuse` dimension. We can show sessions by `socket_origin` (client vs pool) and sampled socket_id to help debug. Current dashboards assume socket_id is unique per session which is false with pooling.

ops-bot: Alert: route eu-west active_sessions/edge_sockets ratio > 1.4 for 10m (threshold 1.2). Incident created: INC-2026-1337.

Leo: Proposal for fix: 1) Emit an additional label on our connection lifecycle events: `socket.origin=pool|client`. 2) Emit `socket.id` consistently so metrics can be attributed at socket granularity. 3) Update console aggregation to dedupe sessions where socket.id shows reuse in < N seconds.

Jo: Also consider a short TTL after client_disconnect before we count the socket as free for dedupe; that helps races where client reconnects quickly. Maybe 5s by default, configurable via edge-config.

Neil: Need to be careful with metrics cardinality. socket.id can explode if we emit for every ephemeral socket. Suggest sampling (1%) for raw socket_id label and always emit socket.origin boolean label. Use the sampled id only for debugging dashboards, not billing paths.

Sarah: Agreed on sampling. For the console UX I can add a column "socket_pool_reuse (sampled %)" and a small toggle to show sampled socket_ids for the selected time-range. That keeps normal dashboards cheap.

Anika: Timeline idea: server-side flag to emit `socket.origin` + sampled `socket.id` behind a feature flag. Canary rollout 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 48h. Update console backend to ingest new label into a new timeseries `edge.socket_origin` (values client,pool,unknown).

Leo: Also: billing/usage pipelines rely on session counts. If we change dedupe rules we could change reported usage. Plan: keep billing pipeline in shadow mode where we compute deduped numbers but do not switch billing. Run comparison for 7 days and then coordinate with finance for cutover.

Jo: For immediate mitigation we can update the console to show both 'active_sessions_by_session_id' and 'active_sockets' side-by-side, with a tooltip explaining pooling behavior. That reduces confusion while we implement telemetry.

Neil: Operational checklist: - add feature flag in edge proxy - ensure label naming is `socket.origin` and `socket.sampled_id` - limit sampled_id sampling rate env var - add docs to observability handbook explaining new labels.

Anika: I'll own the edge proxy change + metrics exporter tests. Will add unit tests that assert label presence and sampling distribution.

Sarah: I'll take the console UX + backend mapping. I'll add a small migration that stores the sampled_id in a debug_index table (non-billed).

Leo: I'll coordinate rollout and the shadow billing run, and notify finance. Proposed schedule: today — implement feature flag + unit tests; tomorrow AM — 5% canary; tomorrow PM — 20%; next day — go wide if no regressions.

Jo: :thumbsup: Also can we add a quick Kibana view that lists socket reuse occurrences by route? That would help on-call triage.

Anika: Good call. I'll add a structured event to the logs (`event=socket_reuse session_id=... socket_origin=pool`) so Kibana queries are straightforward.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: edge-proxy/feat/socket-origin @ 2026-03-23T09:00:00Z (canary 5%).

Leo: Thanks all. One follow-up ask: if anyone sees active_sessions drift during the canary, ping #eng-oncall + tag me. We'll hold rollout if the shadow billing delta > 5% for the canary cohort.

Neil: I'll prep a quick script to compute active_sessions/active_sockets ratio per route so we can baseline before and after.

Sarah: I'll draft the console tooltip text and add a link to the handbook.

Anika: Starting work now — will post PR link when ready.
